title: The Weight of Water
story:
James sat by the edge of the Whispering Brook, his fingers tracing the smooth, cool surface of the sky-blue pebble tucked securely inside his small canvas satchel. James counted three skipping water-striders. James counted four drifting willow leaves. James counted five ripples fading into the grassy bank, a quiet ritual that always brought the restless flutter in his chest to a gentle, steady pace whenever the world felt a little too wide.

He thought of the wildflower-filled meadow behind him, how its bright colors had once seemed like an ocean with no far shore. He thought of the first step he had taken away from home, hesitant and uncertain, and how the earth had simply held his weight without complaint. Every stone had a story, or so he liked to imagine, and today the brook seemed determined to share its own whispered secrets with anyone patient enough to sit completely still and listen.

A sudden splash broke the afternoon quiet, startling a tiny frog from a mossy stone into the rushing current. James watched the water swirl and mend itself, closing over the disturbance as if nothing had ever happened at all. He reached down to adjust the strap of his satchel, feeling the reassuring heft of his single keepsake against his side, a tiny anchor in a landscape that stretched endlessly outward in every direction.

The afternoon light began to lean long and golden across the water, turning the spray into a ribbon of scattered diamonds. James whispered his usual evening phrase to the gathering shadows, a small private greeting to the night, and wondered what sort of morning song the brook would sing when the sun finally came back around to find him.
